record.original_question: For a sequence of integers (x_n) and a fixed digit k, define U_n^(k) to be the position of the digit k in x_n when k occurs and 0 otherwise. Study the sequence U_n^(k) when x_n is the nth prime, n!, or n^n, including questions of convergence and monotonicity, and determine whether these digit-position sequences contain infinitely many prime numbers. Ask the same questions more generally for rational sequences.

evidence.quote: Study {U(k)(pn)}n ... Convergence, monotony. The same questions for the sequences: (2) xn = n!, (3) xn = nn ... Do the sequences of position U(k) contain an infinity of primes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer base $b\ge 2$ and a digit $k\in\{0,1,\dots,b-1\}$. For a positive integer $m$ with base-$b$ representation $m = \sum_{i=0}^{L} d_i b^{i}$ (where $d_L\ne 0$), define the position $P^{(k)}(m)$ of the digit $k$ in $m$ as follows: if $k$ does not occur among the digits $d_0,d_1,\dots,d_L$, set $P^{(k)}(m) = 0$; otherwise let $P^{(k)}(m)$ be the index $i$ of the (say, lowest) position $i$ at which $d_i = k$ (so $P^{(k)}(m)\in\{0,1,\dots,L\}$).

Given a sequence of positive integers $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$, define the digit-position sequence
$$U_n^{(k)} := P^{(k)}(x_n), \qquad n\ge 1.$$

Investigate the following questions for the three sequences
(1) $x_n = p_n$, the $n$-th prime;
(2) $x_n = n!$;
(3) $x_n = n^n$;
and more generally for sequences of rational numbers (interpreting the digit-position via the base-$b$ expansion of numerator and denominator, or of a chosen representation):

(a) Does $(U_n^{(k)})_{n\ge 1}$ converge in any natural sense (e.g.\ in density or in Cesàro average)?
(b) Is $(U_n^{(k)})_{n\ge 1}$ eventually monotone, or does it possess monotone subsequences with prescribed density?
(c) Does the sequence $(U_n^{(k)})_{n\ge 1}$ take prime values infinitely often?

Provide proofs or disproofs of convergence, monotonicity properties, and the infinitude of prime values for each of the cases (1)–(3) and in the general rational setting.
artifact.status_search_result: No published results addressing convergence, monotonicity, or infinitude of primes for the digit-position sequences $U_n^{(k)}$ associated with the $n$-th prime, $n!$, or $n^n$ were located. The problem appears to be a research proposal whose status could not be verified from available sources.
